title: Colours and toys
grammar: It is a… / What colour is…?

scene.speaker: freya
scene.bubble: What's this? It's my toy box! Look — a red ball, a yellow kite… and Pip is hiding inside!
scene.intro: Freya opens her big toy box and — surprise! — everything falls on the floor: a red ball, a yellow kite, three little cars and one sleepy puffin called Pip. Now it is time to put everything back, and that is a game too! Say the name of each toy, say its colour, and count them with Freya. How many toys can YOU find in this unit? Open the box and let's play!

words.clue: It is long and goes on rails. Choo-choo!
It has four wheels. Dad drives it.
It is round. You kick it or throw it.
It flies in the sky on a windy day.
A soft toy bear. You hug it at night.

activities.title: Match the thing with its colour.
Listen to Freya. Write a colour or a number in each gap.

data.script: Nico: Freya, what's in your toy box? … Freya: Look! This is my ball. It's red. … Nico: And what's that? … Freya: It's my kite. It's yellow and very big! … Nico: How many cars have you got? … Freya: I've got three cars. One, two, three! … Nico: And who is this? … Freya: This is my teddy. He's brown. His name is Max. … Nico: And… what's that black and white thing? … Freya: That's not a toy! That's Pip! He's sleeping in my box again!

questions.q: The kite is … and very big.
… is sleeping in the toy box.

activities.title: Exam task · Choose the correct word.

data.instructions: Read and choose the correct word.

items.sentence: It is round. You play football with it.

data.text: Student A points at something in the classroom and asks: "What colour is it?" Student B answers: "It's blue!" Three things each, then swap. Bonus: find something orange!

activities.title: Two toy boxes! Find the differences.

homework.prompt: Draw your 3 favourite toys. Write one sentence for each: This is my ball. It is red.

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.

gramatica: Verb TO BE: I am, You are, He/She is
